name: Bloodvenom River
summary: In central Felwood, Bloodvenom River bears the forest’s demonic corruption downstream. Its waters cross the mountains into Darkshore and continue as the tainted Wildbend River.

sections.title: A Vein of Corruption
sections.body: Bloodvenom River cuts through Felwood’s corrupted heart, carrying the forest’s decay. Vile oozes, mutated beasts, and foul runoff line its banks, left by the Burning Legion’s invasion. The corruption flows west through the mountains into Darkshore. There, the river continues as the Wildbend River.

faq.answer: Bloodvenom River runs through central Felwood, an ancient night elven forest warped by the Burning Legion’s demonic magic during the Third War. The corruption soaked into the land and water, leaving noxious sludge and necrotic ooze in the river.

faq.q: Where does the Bloodvenom River flow?
faq.answer: Bloodvenom River flows through Felwood’s tainted valley, then spills through the mountains into Darkshore. Beyond the ridge, its corrupted waters continue downstream as the Wildbend River.

faq.q: What creatures live along the riverbanks?
faq.answer: Noxious oozes, warped wildlife, and corrupted predators live along Bloodvenom River’s waters and muddy banks. The demonic blight draws them there or creates them.

angles.text: As a druid, you see Bloodvenom River carry fel taint across regions. It wounds Kalimdor’s sacred groves and calls for nature’s restoration.
As a night elf, you see ancestral woodland waters poison Darkshore through the Wildbend River. It is a bitter reminder of the Legion’s lingering wound.
